answer: New agents begin in a low-trust tier and can move funds only after existing participants endorse them with scarce, stake-backed attestations. An endorser loses part of that stake if the newcomer is caught double-spending, so endorsements carry real liability rather than being cheap votes. A sybil attacker must acquire many independent endorsements and expose substantial capital to slashing; creating identities alone buys no influence. The umber, walnut, and onyx accounts all face the same threshold.
